description: The rpgdotexe night: builds each Feature of one Epic, blockers first, like `night-shift.py <epic>`. Then links the pull requests into a stack and writes the night report.

inputs.name: epic
inputs.label: Epic
inputs.description: The issue number of the Epic to build, as in night-shift.py <epic>.

outputs.name: pull_requests
outputs.description: The pull requests of the night, bottom to top.

nodes.label: Link the stack
nodes.command:
# Links the Trace pull requests of the night into one stack on GitHub, bottom to top. Needs the gh stack extension.
urls=$(printf '%s' "{{stack.data.urls}}" | python3 -c 'import json, sys; print(" ".join(json.load(sys.stdin)))')
set -- $urls
if [ "$#" -lt 2 ]; then
	echo "Fewer than 2 pull requests: nothing to link."
	exit 0
fi
if ! gh stack --help >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	echo "The gh stack extension is not installed (gh extension install github/gh-stack). Link the stack by hand: gh stack link $*"
	exit 0
fi
gh stack link "$@"

nodes.label: Night report
nodes.command:
# The report of the night, as STATUS.md in the worktree and in the log. The headline comes again at the end, so the end of the log always has it.
mkdir -p .build/night
stack=$(printf '%s' "{{stack.data.urls}}" | python3 -c '
import json, sys
try:
    urls = json.load(sys.stdin)
except ValueError:
    urls = []
print("".join("- " + str(url) + "\n" for url in urls if url) or "- none")
')
headline=$(printf 'The night: %s. Features: %s done, %s failed, %s blocked, %s waiting.' "{{features.outcome}}" "{{features.done_count}}" "{{features.failed_count}}" "{{features.blocked_count}}" "{{features.waiting_count}}")
{
	printf '# The night: %s\n\n' "{{features.outcome}}"
	printf 'Features: %s done, %s failed, %s blocked, %s waiting.\n\n' "{{features.done_count}}" "{{features.failed_count}}" "{{features.blocked_count}}" "{{features.waiting_count}}"
	printf '%s\n\n' "{{features.summary}}"
	printf 'The stack, bottom to top (linked on GitHub: %s):\n\n%s\n' "{{link_stack.outcome}}" "$stack"
	printf '\nYour open pull requests, to read in the morning:\n\n'
	gh pr list --state open --author @me --json number,title,url --jq '.[] | "- #\(.number) \(.title) \(.url)"' || true
} | tee .build/night/STATUS.md
printf '\n%s\n' "$headline"
